title: Are Heat Pumps a Scam?
summary: Undecided tests common heat pump myths on cost, cold performance, running cost versus gas, ductwork and reliability, concluding the answer depends on local prices and installs.

assertions.quote: heat pumps can be more than 100% efficient. They can deliver more thermal energy than the electrical energy they consume.
modern heat pumps work in temperatures down to -26°C
Low temperatures used to be a problem, but newer iterations of ASHPs implement multiple strategies to keep themselves running during extreme weather.
Air-source heat pumps tend to be much cheaper than geothermal ones.
even highly efficient heat pumps can cost more to operate than a gas furnace.
Eversource has a winter rate program that cuts distribution and transmission costs by about 23% from November through April.
The most important thing to know about the cost of any heat pump is that it’s extremely variable.

verdicts.note: Installed prices vary with system type, capacity, ductwork, electrical work and regional labour costs.

assertions.quote: out of 365 days a year, there’s four to seven days of temperatures that force the backup heating system to kick on
So even when heat pumps have to work harder in colder climates, you’re still getting better performance than you would with fossil fuels.

verdicts.note: With a COP above 1 a heat pump delivers more heat per unit of site energy than a furnace, but per unit of primary energy or cost the edge narrows or reverses in deep cold.
Cold-climate units keep COP of 2 or more at 5F, beating any furnace, but when the load exceeds capacity backup resistance at COP 1 takes over.
RMI's cold-climate heat pump keeps a site COP of 1.4 at -13F, above the 0.85-0.95 efficiency it assumes for fossil furnaces (site energy, not primary energy).
Heat-pump-only cycles kept COP about 1.3 even at the 10F change point, while measured propane furnace cycles ran about 57-85% efficient.

Field COPs averaged about 1.5 at -10 to 0 F, while the report puts fuel heating's equivalent COP at its system efficiency of 0.7 to 0.9; this holds per unit of site energy, not counting power-plant losses.
A median COP of 1.9 at 0-5 F (1.6-2.7 below 30 F) beats any furnace's site efficiency below 1.0; this compares site energy only and comes from pre-commercial prototypes.

assertions.quote: a heat pump is only as reliable as its installer

verdicts.note: Installation faults are common (DOE and NIST find most HVAC systems have at least one), but equipment defects and defrost problems also cause failures.

assertions.quote: In most places across the States, you can swap your central AC or furnace with an ASHP, no ducts required.
